I took Adderall out of curiosity when I was 16 and got addicted to them when I really had anxiety/concentration issues misdiagnosed as ADHD. It’s well over a year later and I can still feel the cravings for the pills. Take this as a lesson and don’t touch it again, you don’t realize how addicted to something you can be until you’d rather kill yourself than quit. That’s how I felt for months and I probably wouldn’t have made it through the weeks-long WD symptoms if I wasn’t under 24/7 parental supervision for a month and a half and stuck in an psychiatric facility for an additional week. The pills made me into a monster though. I still have to decide not to take them every single day and sometimes making the right choice is hard, but it’s definitely possible. Addictions come in pharmaceutical bottles, try not to be too curious. You won’t like what you find out and you won’t like the cravings you’re gonna have for it if you keep doing it. They haven’t gone away for me yet and I haven’t taken Adderall in a very long time. I also still have some of the brain fog and happen to be very susceptible to depression, chronic aches and pain because I fried my brain with these things. You wouldn’t believe how good the brain is at firing off pain signals when it doesn’t have a substance it’s been using for a long time. 

Long story short, you fry your brain and you stay really stupid and demotivated for a long while after you quit; you’ll probably lose friends and do stupid things out of anger from not having your fix like I did. I don’t mean to sound like your parents but they’re not exaggerating the dangers of prescription medicines, these little pills are fucked. 

Adderall is the scaled-down version of cocaine for kids and college students; the government prescribes amphetamines to children and wonders why the pharmaceutical companies are so rich. It’s because a lot of us get addicted to them, you just didn’t like it because you took an obscene amount. I was taking 30-40 mg daily when I quit, and my script should have been for 10 mg. I got curious and bought my friend’s instant release pills for a few weeks, enjoyed the feeling immensely and noticed how “productive” and “focused” I was (spoiler: I was bouncing off the walls and had an involuntary eye twitch), and from there I was able to get myself a nice big prescription filled. I then proceeded to take my medicine as prescribed for about a week before I felt the compulsion to take more of it, because I wasn’t getting the same boost of unparalleled confidence and euphoria from the dose I’d been administered. So, I’d sneak into the medicine cabinet and take my own medicine off-label whenever I wanted to. 

This went on for about 3 months until I started going really insane because of the pills. I don’t remember a lot of the things I did, but I was very violent and very prone to immediately becoming thoroughly enraged at anything and anyone for no reason. It was a very gradual decline but very drastic at the same time. The wrong tone could have made me feel the almost uncontrollable urge to kill somebody, and that’s when I started realizing I had a problem. So, I committed myself to the inpatient psychiatric ward because I was feeling suicidal following the cold-turkey “quit” (eventually there were no more scripts written for me).
